# Infantry AI

> Infantry AI is a command post for coding agents: a daemon with a ticket board, agents on their own git branches, mail, shared project knowledge, Lua scripts and hooks, plus desktop, web, Android and CLI clients. The core is small and generic; every feature is a plugin (a module with a `module.json`). Core is MPL-2.0, everything else Apache-2.0.

Read AGENTS.md first. Facts in these docs come from the code; where an older design record disagrees, the code wins.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the guide for AI coding agents: rules, repo layout, build and test commands, where each change goes.
- [Architecture](docs/wiki/Architecture.md): the three layers, the daemon, the protocol, the request flow from a click to the daemon and back, slots and child plugins, scripting.
- [Recipes](docs/wiki/recipes/README.md): worked "how to add X" guides with the exact files to touch.

## Build plugins

- [Make a plugin](docs/wiki/make-a-plugin.md): from the template to a built UI + daemon example; every `module.json` field.
- [Plugins](docs/wiki/Plugins.md): module tiers, panels and slots, config, building, installing, signing.
- [UI plugin API](docs/wiki/plugin-api.md): every public type of the UI plugin API.
- [Daemon plugin API](docs/wiki/daemon-plugin-api.md): tools, routes, hooks, events, services, storage, the guard.
- [Harnesses and providers](docs/wiki/Harnesses.md): adding an agent CLI and a model group.
- [Kotlin notes](docs/wiki/kotlin-notes.md): toolchain versions, UI core source sets and expect/actual, Compose MP pitfalls, why incremental is off.

## Automate and configure

- [Scripting](docs/wiki/Scripting.md): the Lua API, hooks, the process bridge, settings that govern scripts.
- [Board and epics](docs/wiki/Board.md): epics, and moving tickets between epics.
- [Settings](docs/wiki/Settings.md): scopes (app, project, role, session) and cost-saving defaults.

## Project

- [README](README.md): install and first run.
- [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): building, branches, testing.
- [Licensing](docs/wiki/licensing.md): what is MPL-2.0 and what is Apache-2.0, per module.
